homily:
Imagine a doorway. We all know the feeling of standing before one—perhaps it is the front door of a house where you once felt completely at home, or an airport gate where you waited for a flight that would take you somewhere beautiful. There is a specific kind of anticipation in those moments. You are waiting for something to happen, for someone to appear, for the threshold to be crossed. In our reading from Ephesians, Saint Paul speaks of a much greater doorway. He tells us that in Christ, the dividing walls—the things that keep us apart, the things that make us feel like strangers or sojourners—have been broken down. He says, 'For he is our peace, he made both one.'

Think of the way Benjamin loved to watch the skies. He didn’t just look at airplanes; he studied them. He understood the complex systems that hold a massive Boeing 737 in the air, the invisible currents and the precise engineering that allow a machine to traverse the globe. He had this brilliant, sharp mind that sought to understand how things are held together. And yet, the most beautiful thing about Benjamin wasn’t his intellect, as vast as it was. It was his capacity to be at home in the world and to make others feel at home with him. He was a boy who could navigate the complexities of technology and the complexities of human relationships with the same gentle, steady heart.

There is a deep, aching truth we must name today: the world can feel very empty when someone we love is no longer walking through the door. For Alan and Thao, for Ryan, the house might feel quiet in a way that is hard to bear. You might find yourself listening for a footstep, or looking at the spot where he used to stand, or remembering the way he would giggle when he talked about his 'con chim airlines.' That ache is real. It is not a sign that you have failed or that you have lost your way. It is a sign of how deeply you loved him. When we lose someone who was the light of our lives, the world feels like it has lost its center of gravity. You might wonder if you are doing enough, or if you are carrying the weight correctly. But hear this: you are not alone in the silence. The God who built the universe, the God who holds the stars in their places, is the same God who holds Benjamin in His arms.

In the Gospel, Jesus tells us to 'gird your loins and light your lamps.' He is telling us to be ready, to be vigilant. This isn't a command to be anxious or to worry about the future. It is an invitation to keep our hearts open and our spirits ready for the unexpected ways God shows up in our lives. Often, we think of 'being ready' as something we do for the end of our lives, but it is actually about how we live today. It is about keeping the lamp of love lit, even when the night feels long. It is about recognizing that even in our grief, God is at the door, knocking gently, waiting to be invited into the room of our sorrow.

Do you remember how Benjamin was always ready to offer what he had? That moment when he offered his entire piggy bank for his uncle—he didn't have to do that. He wasn't asked. He simply saw a need and his heart moved toward it. That is the heart of a disciple. That is the heart of someone who is already living in the Kingdom. He didn't need to empty the bank; the offer itself was the treasure. And that is what God asks of us today. He doesn't ask us to fix our grief or to pretend we aren't hurting. He asks us to offer our hearts, just as they are—broken, tired, hopeful, or confused—and to let Him walk through the door of our lives.

Ryan, your brother loved you more than words can capture. You were his partner in every sense. When you look at the sky and see a plane, or when you sit in the quiet, know that you are not just remembering a past; you are connected to a living reality. Benjamin is not far off. He is in the 'household of God,' just as Paul describes, a fellow citizen with the holy ones. He is not a stranger to you; he is a part of the foundation upon which your own life is being built. Your life, your future, your dreams—they are all part of the same structure that God is building, a temple sacred in the Lord.

If you are feeling the weight of the day, if the morning light brings a fresh wave of missing him, turn your eyes to the 'capstone.' Jesus is the one who holds it all together. He is the one who reconciles, who heals, who makes the two into one. When you feel that you cannot go on, remember that you are being built together into a dwelling place of God. You are not just a collection of memories; you are a living, breathing part of God’s plan. And Benjamin is there, cheering you on, his smile still radiating the joy he always carried.

What can you carry out the door today? Just this: the promise that you are never truly alone. When you feel the silence, speak a name. When you feel the ache, offer it as a prayer. When you see something beautiful—a plane in the sky, a bird in flight, a moment of kindness—remember that this is a glimpse of the world Benjamin is now experiencing in its fullness. You are a family held by God. You are seen, you are known, and you are loved beyond measure. Keep your lamps lit by small acts of kindness, by continuing to love one another, and by trusting that the Master of the house is not only returning—He is already here, waiting to sit at the table with you and to give you rest. May you feel the peace that passes all understanding, and may the memory of Benjamin’s gentle spirit be the light that guides you home, one step at a time.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that You are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love You above all things, and I desire to receive You into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive You sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace You as if You were already there and unite myself wholly to You. Never permit me to be separated from You. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you in His peace, now and forever. Amen.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text: Brothers and sisters: You were at that time without Christ, alienated from the community of Israel and strangers to the covenants of promise, without hope and without God in the world. But now in Christ Jesus you who once were far off have become near by the Blood of Christ. For he is our peace, he made both one and broke down the dividing wall of enmity, through his Flesh, abolishing the law with its commandments and legal claims, that he might create in himself one new person in place of the two, thus establishing peace, and might reconcile both with God, in one Body, through the cross, putting that enmity to death by it. He came and preached peace to you who were far off and peace to those who were near, for through him we both have access in one Spirit to the Father. So then you are no longer strangers and sojourners, but you are fellow citizens with the holy ones and members of the household of God, built upon the foundation of the Apostles and prophets, with Christ Jesus himself as the capstone. Through him the whole structure is held together and grows into a temple sacred in the Lord; in him you also are being built together into a dwelling place of God in the Spirit.

readings.label: Responsorial Psalm
readings.text: R. The Lord speaks of peace to his people. I will hear what God proclaims; the LORD–for he proclaims peace. Near indeed is his salvation to those who fear him, glory dwelling in our land. R. The Lord speaks of peace to his people. Kindness and truth shall meet; justice and peace shall kiss. Truth shall spring out of the earth, and justice shall look down from heaven. R. The Lord speaks of peace to his people. The LORD himself will give his benefits; our land shall yield its increase. Justice shall walk before him, and salvation, along the way of his steps. R. The Lord speaks of peace to his people.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text: Jesus said to his disciples: “Gird your loins and light your lamps and be like servants who await their master’s return from a wedding, ready to open immediately when he comes and knocks. Blessed are those servants whom the master finds vigilant on his arrival. Amen, I say to you, he will gird himself, have them recline at table, and proceed to wait on them. And should he come in the second or third watch and find them prepared in this way, blessed are those servants.”

day: Tuesday of the Twenty-ninth Week in Ordinary Time

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben - Been dreaming about you a lot. Hope you're having fun up in heaven. Please look after our family. Remember to come say hi daily. We miss you so much!

Ben ơi, trong giấc ngủ anh Huy đã thấy Ben về thăm anh, trao cho anh lời cầu nguyện để hai anh em mình lại được tìm thấy nhau. Xin Chúa thương nhậm lời Ben, cho Ben được hưởng ngàn thu bình an bên Chúa. Nếu có thể, xin Ben lại ghé thăm anh trong những giấc mơ tiếp theo nhé, dù chỉ là một lời chào hay một nụ cười thân thương như ngày nào.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Ben, my sweet boy, I miss you so much. Thank you for visiting me and Chú Chris last night. He told me he saw you flying a helicopter—so free, joyful, and strong up there. Down here, Mom and I are crying more and more each day. A piece of my heart feels completely dead without you, Ben. Please watch over us, pray for your mom, your brother Ryan, and me, and give us the strength to keep going. We love you forever

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Today marks 100 days without you. Miss you a whole a lot Ben. Feel free to visit any time! See you around buddy! Love you!

Ben ơi, nay anh M đi xử lý hồ sơ ở Cam Ranh, đi ngang qua Cam Ranh Airport. Rồi cuộc nói chuyện về máy bay của Ben lại ùa về, nhớ nhiều kỷ niệm về Ben lắm ( anh M sẽ giữ kín kakaka). Quỷ nhỏ, tự nhiên nghĩ về mày buồn dễ sợ. Hãy đi đến những nơi mà Ben muốn nha và đừng quên là luôn nhớ về gia đình mình nhé, thương em trai nhiều. Giá như !!!!!!!!!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: What happened my son? It's been 3 months since you left us. Missing you so much my whole body aches. Mom cries every day now... What are we going to do now Ben?  Please pray for us.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text:
Hey Ben,

Rafael Rizzo and his little brother Ben really need your help right now. Please bless them with good health and give them the strength to get through this together. Please watch over Brandon and Flor's health, too.

I miss you a whole bunch. I know you're up in heaven watching over all of us. Whenever you're able to, stop by to visit, yeah? I love you and miss you so much!
